facts.fact: Independent News reports that 38 Tinkhundla centres, with 859 schools and 134 health centres, are set to benefit from broadband connectivity under the E1.2 billion (USD 65 million) World Bank-funded digitisation project, whose rollout is expected in 2027; the figure is a planned target, none is reported connected, and no total of Tinkhundla centres is given.
facts.system: Eswatini Digitization Project (Digital Eswatini): broadband connectivity for Tinkhundla centres

facts.fact: Of the project's E1.2 billion, E648 million is allocated to affordable broadband expansion, comprising EPTC stabilisation and reform, fibre network expansion and last-mile connectivity, under which 38 Tinkhundla centres are to be connected; rollout is expected in 2027, as reported on 24 June 2026.
facts.system: Eswatini Digitization Project (Digital Eswatini): broadband connectivity for Tinkhundla centres

facts.fact: The E1.2 billion (USD 65 million) project that is to bring broadband to 38 Tinkhundla centres is funded through a World Bank loan, as reported on 24 June 2026; no domestic budget line is stated.
facts.system: Eswatini Digitization Project (Digital Eswatini): broadband connectivity for Tinkhundla centres

facts.fact: The Ministry of ICT, through the Digital Eswatini Project Implementation Unit, is preparing the project and ran a three-day change-agent training workshop in Mbabane from 23 June 2026 for officials from across ministries and institutions.
facts.system: Eswatini Digitization Project (Digital Eswatini): broadband connectivity for Tinkhundla centres
